events.title: Storming of the Bastille
events.description: A crowd of Parisian revolutionaries stormed the Bastille, a royal fortress and prison in Paris, seizing weapons and gunpowder and freeing the few prisoners held there.
events.significance: The event became the symbol of the start of the French Revolution and the fall of absolute monarchy in France. It is commemorated annually as Bastille Day, France's national holiday.

events.title: Death of Billy the Kid
events.description: Outlaw Henry McCarty, known as Billy the Kid, was shot and killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett at Fort Sumner in the New Mexico Territory.
events.significance: His death ended one of the most famous outlaw careers of the American Old West and cemented his legendary status in American folklore and popular culture.

events.title: Mariner 4 Flyby of Mars
events.description: NASA's Mariner 4 spacecraft completed the first successful flyby of Mars, returning the first close-up images of the planet's surface.
events.significance: The images revealed a cratered, barren landscape and changed scientific understanding of Mars, marking a milestone in interplanetary exploration.

events.title: Iraqi Revolution
events.description: Army officers led by Abd al-Karim Qasim and Abdul Salam Arif overthrew the Hashemite monarchy in Iraq, killing King Faisal II and others in the royal family.
events.significance: The coup ended the monarchy and established the Iraqi Republic, reshaping Middle Eastern politics and Iraq's alignment during the Cold War.

events.title: Nice Truck Attack
events.description: On Bastille Day, a truck was driven into crowds celebrating on the Promenade des Anglais in Nice, France, killing 86 people and injuring hundreds.
events.significance: One of the deadliest terrorist attacks in modern French history, it led to extended states of emergency and intensified security measures across Europe.
